title: Refuse in the Tool, Not in the Prompt
tagline: Move a broken rule into the tool. Do this only where the tool can check the rule.

story.problem: A scout recorded a caterer with the inquiry address inquiries@hideseekmedia.com. The scout read the address from a WeddingWire page for a different business. Outreach runs live. Thus one more plan could send a wedding inquiry to the inbox of a real stranger. The scout's instructions already forbid directory sources, and they already require a published address on the vendor's own site.
story.solution: record_vendor refuses at the write boundary. The tool refuses a source URL on one of 20 known directories; the check matches host labels, not substrings of the URL. The tool refuses an email whose corporate domain shares nothing with the vendor's name or website; free mail passes untouched. The tool refuses a source page that returns a definitive 404 or 410. Each refusal returns a note that names the next action. The tool also applies the counter-lesson: a required drive time, which no tool in the system can produce, became an optional field. The instructions tell the scout never to search for a drive time. When the prose rule lost its effect under measurement, the radius returned as arithmetic. record_vendor geocodes the vendor's town and the couple's town. The tool refuses a vendor beyond the straight-line miles that the stated drive covers, and it passes each vendor that it cannot judge.
story.outcome: The guards have unit tests that use real rows from a production run and no model. The findings that the scout eval caught get a rejection. Each legitimate finding from the same run continues to pass, which includes gmail addresses and contact-form-only vendors. After the removal of the unreachable drive-time requirement, the eval read 52/53, with the radius judge at 100% on the day of the measurement. A later settled run measured the failure of the prose rule. The distance guard's first runs read five refusals, with each recorded vendor within 38 straight-line miles, then 49/54 (91%) with 13 of 14 within 40.

prerequisites: This repository cloned and npm install run once
Network access: the liveness guard issues one real GET per recorded vendor
No model key for the guard suite — the checks are pure functions plus one fetch
No local key for npm run eval:scout either — it drives the deployed Venus, whose keys live on the deployment

quickstart.configure: npm install — the guard suite needs no API key; add .env.local only if you go on to npm run eval:scout
